edits.title: Reuse a URL-keyed evidence cache for table extraction
edits.content: For a bounded table-research task, keep fetched text in a URL-keyed dictionary. Deduplicate candidate URLs and exclude cached URLs before batching fetches; retain successful responses and exclude failed responses from extraction evidence. Supply cached URL/text pairs together to a schema-validated extraction call. Use the same cache to verify that every cited URL was fetched and every nonempty quotation occurs verbatim in its cited text. Check source hostnames with exact-domain or dot-delimited subdomain matching, then verify exact requested row coverage and cell keys before recording constraint checks. Cache reuse avoids another backend fetch. These checks establish intermediate evidence consistency; they do not by themselves establish successful final submission.

edits.title: Diagnose missing biographical fields before further research
edits.content: When structured extraction leaves a biographical field empty, review the stored source specifically for explicit evidence of that field. Distinguish source absence from extraction omission. Do not derive nationality or citizenship from birthplace, education, or workplace. If evidence is absent, retain the unresolved field and search for a source explicitly stating the requested attribute; fetch and verify that evidence before filling the cell. For affiliations, distinguish employment and secondary appointments from educational institutions, and preserve temporal qualifiers such as former or emeritus. Give extraction and review calls the same field definition, time scope, and completeness requirements. If the task uses affiliations recorded in an award announcement, audit those institutions and their stated locations rather than expanding to every outside appointment. Resolve concrete omissions against stored evidence before further searches. Apply this review to unresolved fields without repeating successful searches or downloads.

edits.title: Compare repair results with existing evidence before replacement
edits.content: A targeted re-extraction using only newly fetched sources replaced a supported multi-valued nationality with a narrower value from another person's page navigation. Schema and quote-membership checks passed despite the information loss; recovery required restoring the stronger stored evidence. Supply repair calls with the existing cell and its supporting evidence alongside new evidence. Before replacement, compare source relevance, temporal scope, and every removed or changed component. A source mentioning only one component does not refute the others. Preserve supported components unless evidence justifies their removal, and keep unresolved conflicts explicit. Failed fetches do not invalidate evidence already collected.

proposal.summary: Refine discovery identity handling and evidence-completeness checks. Existing fetch-recovery guidance remains supported.

edits.title: Inspect discoveries and reconcile name variants
edits.content: Empty discovery placeholders can cause stalled_search signals even when later calls record entities. After each search, inspect its results and record actual newly discovered entities once; for search_many, handle each query in input order. Compare identities rather than raw name strings: reconcile supported variants involving initials, shortened names, or apostrophe styles with existing entities before recording discoveries. Keep aliases as evidence metadata, not new entities; do not merge ambiguous names without supporting context. Use [] honestly when no new entities were found, including searches that successfully verify fields for known entities. Such searches can advance evidence coverage despite a stalled_search signal. Never invent discoveries to suppress a warning.

edits.title: Recover and validate incomplete rendered evidence
edits.content: When a model-rendered fetch returns usable but incomplete text, identify the specific missing fields before fetching again. Request concise factual summaries with brief supporting excerpts instead of full-page reproduction. Test the revised focus on one page and inspect the evidence before expanding. Preserve each response with its URL and focus. Keep unstated fields unresolved and use alternative sources rather than inferring facts from birthplace, institutional location, or ambiguous collective descriptions. Validate quotations against an individual saved response, then separately review whether they support the correct entity, field, time, and required scope. A nonempty value and matching quotation do not establish completeness: track summaries, truncated excerpts, and unresolved attribution as outstanding gaps. For exact wording, retrieve the complete required statement; do not insert editorial gap notes into factual values. Preserve shared attribution when applying a statement to multiple entities. Give reviewers the actual contract, including whether quotations must match rendered responses or original page text, and each field's time scope. Repair concrete defects, rerun structural and quotation checks, and review the repaired fields before submission. FETCH_FAILED requires the separate bounded retry and source-switching procedure.

additional_candidates.description: Raw-string novelty counted name variants of known entities as new discoveries.
Semantic review recovered incomplete statements and attribution defects that passed quotation membership and nonempty-cell checks.

decisions.reason: All 16 occurrences concern follow-up research on already discovered entities: six year-level nationality queries, three targeted affiliation/nationality queries, four individual nationality queries, and three final audit queries. Their empty discovery records are consistent with verification rather than failed discovery; several supplied evidence used in the final output. Existing memory explicitly permits honest empty records for verification. Repeated signals across recorded outcomes therefore do not establish that this guidance is ineffective.

Reviewed all 21 failures: ten initial Nobel-domain requests, two early alternative-source failures, three nationality-source failures, two later university/news failures, two biography/CV failures, and two final Nature failures. The run excluded attempted URLs, tested a small alternative-domain batch, reused saved hits, and recovered through other sources, including an alternate CV and a professional-society announcement. Existing memory covers this procedure and cautions against attributing failures to URL formatting. The outcomes show recovery rather than consistently harmful guidance; neither a permanent domain blacklist nor another retry rule is justified.

The discovery log counts omitted initials, added middle initials, apostrophe variants, and surnames alone as new entities after their full identities were already recorded. The trajectory's raw-string known_names comparison explains this inflation. Final rows avoided duplication, but the discovery bookkeeping failure remains reusable and belongs in the existing discovery memory.

Quotation checks repeatedly passed while a motivation remained truncated; later, even 'Missing cells: []' coexisted with an editorial note admitting incomplete evidence. Semantic audits identified this and attribution problems, and targeted retrieval repaired them before the successful final review. Earlier reviewers also questioned original-page quotation fidelity despite the rendered-text contract. Extend the existing recovery skill with separate completeness tracking and contract-aligned review rather than creating overlapping guidance. Its empty usage/outcome history provides no basis for deletion.

proposal.summary: Update one existing memory to prevent nationality/citizenship drift and unsupported audit corrections. Existing entries already cover fetch failures and honest empty discovery records.

edits.title: Separate quote membership from factual support
edits.content: A quote occurring in model-rendered fetch output does not by itself establish that it is a source quotation or supports the complete claim. Distinguish source excerpts from renderer summaries, headings, labels and assembled passages; do not reject an identified source excerpt solely because the fetch tool renders it. Before recording a positive constraint verdict, verify the entity, required time period and every substantive component of the value against appropriate evidence. Keep extraction and audit criteria aligned with the requested column: explicit national descriptors can support nationality without proving legal citizenship or dual citizenship. Birthplace, ancestry, workplace, flags and unlinked country labels are insufficient substitutes. Preserve explicitly supported compound national descriptors without converting them into citizenship claims. Treat model audit findings as hypotheses to check against saved evidence, not authoritative corrections; distinguish actual additional affiliations from parenthetical organizational descriptions. When different sources support different parts of a composite claim, retain an internal mapping from each claim to its source excerpt and respect the output contract rather than stitching excerpts into a purported verbatim quote. Recheck semantic support after final mutations, even when schema, substring and coverage checks pass.

additional_candidates.description: Extraction and review repeatedly conflated nationality with citizenship, and some audit findings rejected rendered excerpts or demanded a parent organization without establishing a separate affiliation.

decisions.reason: All 29 occurrences correspond to empty discovery records: four fallback searches returned already discovered names, nine nationality searches verified known people, eleven gap searches sought missing fields, and five final searches targeted remaining cells. These searches produced useful evidence despite adding no entities. The trajectory inspected results before recording discoveries, unlike the premature-placeholder failure described in the existing memory. Entry 0 already explicitly permits honest empty records for verification searches. Its repeated signal-bearing outcomes therefore do not establish that its procedure is ineffective, and no additional warning or instruction to invent discoveries is warranted.

Reviewed all 26 failures: nine initial NobelPrize.org requests, six initial alternative-source requests, seven nationality requests, two gap requests and two final targeted requests. The nationality batch retried previously failed LIGO and AP URLs; an APS URL that previously succeeded also failed, so neither permanent host outages nor malformed suffixes are established. Two KVA probes succeeded and alternative sources subsequently supported completion. Current entry 1 was already revised to require availability probes before large batches, preserve successful evidence, track failed URLs and avoid unchanged retries. Its usage records concern version 1, not the current version 2; these outcomes do not justify deleting or rewriting the revised procedure. The passing self-check does not erase the wasted requests, but another edit would duplicate existing coverage.

The second audit demanded explicit citizenship for a nationality column; later prompts corrected that criterion and restored an explicitly supported compound national descriptor. Reviews also challenged rendered name–institution lines and later demanded a parent organization as an additional affiliation; focused resolution retained the existing two-institution value. These recoveries show that audit output itself needs evidence checking. Entry 3 already covers quotation provenance and semantic support, but does not clearly distinguish nationality from legal citizenship or guard against unsupported audit corrections. Its update preserves that coverage and adds these specific failure modes. Successful substring checks and complete agent-verdict coverage do not independently validate the reviewers' semantic criteria. Entry 2's saved-evidence repair guidance remains useful and needs no separate edit.

edits.title: Supplement missing biographical fields with field-specific evidence
edits.content: For award-recipient tables, extract names, award years, award-time affiliations and individual prize motivations from official award announcements. Preserve distinct motivations for split awards. Keep unsupported fields explicitly unresolved. Build targeted biography searches only for missing fields and group related entities for schema-validated extraction, retaining each source URL and original fetched text. Nationality requires an explicit nationality or citizenship statement; birthplace, ancestry, residence and institutional location are not substitutes. Preserve supported multiple nationalities and the source's regional or historical qualifications. Do not silently convert a historical state designation into present citizenship. Validate each nonempty quote as an exact contiguous substring of every source cited for that quote, then separately verify that the passage supports the complete value for the correct person and requested time. Exact membership alone does not establish semantic support. Use supplementary biographies only for the missing field rather than replacing already supported award facts. Merge verified cells into the existing rows and retain unresolved cases for focused follow-up.

Record 71 checks exact substring membership, but record 76 converts a nationality label containing a historical state and a parenthetical successor into an unqualified modern nationality value. Membership passes without resolving that interpretation. Record 75 instead preserves a regional designation. These observations justify retaining historical and regional qualifications and checking semantic support separately from quote membership. This is folded into the supplementation skill rather than creating another entry or asserting an answer correction.
